# Conceptual Data Model

## Definition

A Conceptual Data Model identifies the business things of interest and their high-level relationships, without technical detail and independent of any implementation.

## Explanation

It fixes **scope** and **vocabulary**: which [[Business Concept|business concepts]] are in view and how they relate. It is the first data model to be agreed with business stakeholders and a key input to the [[Information Model]]. Every entity should trace to a governed concept ([[Concept-to-Model Traceability]]).

## Distinctions

- Versus [[Semantic Model]]: a conceptual model shows *which* concepts and relationships matter; the semantic model states *precisely what they mean* (definitions, identity criteria, specialization, equivalence). In many practices these are merged; this knowledge base keeps them separate (see [[Architecture Layer]]).
- Versus [[Logical Data Model]]: no keys, no normalization, no paradigm.

## Examples

- "A Customer holds one or more Agreements; an Agreement covers one or more Products."
